facts.content: Patient presents with an acute left-sided headache that started around midday today and is associated with nausea and vomiting.
facts.source_text: CC: acute left-sided headache starting around midday today; associated with nausea/vomiting.

facts.content: The headache is unilateral, throbbing, and located on the left side.
facts.source_text: HPI: unilateral throbbing pain on the left

facts.content: The headache is worsened by movement and neck flexion.
The headache was preceded by a visual aura described as zigzag lines with blurred vision.
facts.source_text: preceded by visual aura (zigzag lines) with blurred vision

facts.content: The patient reports photophobia associated with the headache.
Vision is affected in both eyes during the headache episode.
The patient has vomited twice today in association with the headache.
The patient reports no fever with the current headache.
The patient had a similar headache a few weeks ago that lasted a couple of days.
facts.source_text: Similar headache a few weeks ago lasting a couple days.

facts.content: The patient is experiencing stress at work.
Findings per history include aura with unilateral left throbbing headache, photophobia, nausea, vomiting, and no reported focal neurological symptoms.
facts.source_text: Findings per history: aura with unilateral left throbbing headache; photophobia; N/V; no focal neuro symptoms reported.

facts.content: There is no documented past medical history for the patient.
There are no prior migraines noted in this patient.
facts.source_text: no prior migraines noted in patient.

facts.content: The patient has been taking the combined oral contraceptive Microgynon for three months.
facts.source_text: Meds: Microgynon (combined oral contraceptive) for 3 months.

facts.content: No allergies are noted for the patient.
The patient's mother has migraines.
The patient's mother has underactive thyroid.
The patient lives alone.
The patient is a non-smoker.
The patient does not consume alcohol.
The patient does no regular exercise.
Vital signs are not provided.
Physical examination is not documented.
The patient reports no speech difficulty.
The patient reports no limb weakness.
The patient reports no balance disturbance.
The patient reports no head trauma.
The primary assessment is probable migraine with aura presenting as unilateral left-sided headache with photophobia, nausea, vomiting, and visual aura.
facts.source_text: 1) Probable migraine with aura presenting as unilateral left-sided headache with photophobia, N/V, and visual aura.

facts.content: No red flags are evident from the history for the current headache.
facts.source_text: No red flags evident from history.

facts.content: The patient has anxiety about having a brain tumor and was reassured after the history.
facts.source_text: 2) Anxiety about brain tumor; patient reassured after history.

facts.content: Stress-related factors at work are noted, and coping is to be addressed.
facts.source_text: 3) Stress-related factors at work; coping to be addressed.

facts.content: For acute treatment, consider analgesia with paracetamol or cocodamol and NSAIDs such as ibuprofen or naproxen for relief.
facts.source_text: Acute treatment: consider analgesia with paracetamol or cocodamol; NSAIDs (ibuprofen or naproxen) for relief.

facts.content: If headaches persist or worsen, prophylactic options will be discussed at the next visit.
facts.source_text: If headaches persist or worsen: discuss prophylactic options at next visit.

facts.content: The patient is to start a headache diary to capture triggers, aura, and response to treatment.
facts.source_text: Symptom monitoring: start headache diary to capture triggers, aura, and response to treatment.

facts.content: Safety net advice includes returning immediately if the headache worsens or is not improving in 2–3 days, if neck pain worsens, if new weakness in arms or legs develops, or if new vision changes occur.
facts.source_text: Safety net: return immediately if headache worsens or not improving in 2–3 days; if neck pain worsens; new weakness in arms/legs; or new vision changes.

facts.content: The use of the combined oral contraceptive Microgynon will be discussed as part of the migraine discussion, including a review of risks and benefits.
facts.source_text: Contraception: discuss combined oral contraceptive use (Microgynon) as part of migraine discussion; review risks/benefits.

facts.content: The patient is planned to be seen next week to reassess and adjust therapy as needed.
facts.source_text: Follow-up: plan to see next week to reassess and adjust therapy as needed.
